newsitem.title: USA: AFL-CIO to give Teamsters strike aid.
newsitem.headline: AFL-CIO to give Teamsters strike aid.

text.p: The AFL-CIO will announce financial support Tuesday for the 185,000 Teamsters on strike against United Parcel Service, a source familiar with the situation said.

"Yes, that will be announced," said the source, who asked not to be identified. The aid will be announced at a joint news conference with Teamsters President Ron Carey and John Sweeney, president of the AFL-CIO labour group, at 12:30 p.m. EDT (1630 GMT), the source added.
The aid was beinge announced as the strike against UPS began to turn bitter.

UPS Chief Executive James Kelly warned that 15,000 Teamsters would lose their jobs if the strike lasts two weeks. The company said also took out full-page ads in 44 newspapers, telling its side of the story and accusing the Teamsters of prolonging the strike.
Labour Secretary Alexis Herman on Monday asked both sides to be flexible and compromise. The company's top negotiator said after meeting with her that it is sticking by its pre-strike offer.
